content.text:
Upstream OrcaSlicer offers 23 interface languages. That count comes from the current upstream `main` branch (fetched today, commit `3bfabc9831`). Only three of the 23 are tied to a specific region. Every other language has a single version with no regional variants.

The language picker in Preferences, in `src/slic3r/GUI/Preferences.cpp`, lists 24 languages in the code. It only shows a language that also has a translation catalog in `localization/i18n/`. Romanian is in the code's list but has no catalog, so people never see it. That leaves these 23:

- **English**: the source language, which also has its own catalog.
- **Three regional variants**:
  - Simplified Chinese (zh_CN)
  - Traditional Chinese (zh_TW)
  - Brazilian Portuguese (pt_BR)
- **Nineteen languages with no region**:
  - Basque
  - Catalan
  - Czech
  - Dutch
  - French
  - German
  - Hungarian
  - Italian
  - Japanese
  - Korean
  - Lithuanian
  - Polish
  - Russian
  - Spanish
  - Swedish
  - Thai
  - Turkish
  - Ukrainian
  - Vietnamese

Chinese has two versions, Simplified and Traditional, and they are separate catalogs. Portuguese exists only as Brazilian Portuguese; there is no European Portuguese. English and Spanish each have a single version with no regional variants.

I checked the catalog folders and the picker's list. I did not open each catalog to see how complete its translation is, so some languages may still have many untranslated strings.

agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md:111:**Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build JusPrin translation catalogs from OrcaSlicer's .po files.

OrcaSlicer names itself in about 85 user-facing strings and in every
translation of them. Rather than editing those source strings (and the
translation macros) in upstream files, this script produces the catalogs the
application loads, with the product name substituted:

  * one <lang>/<domain>.mo per upstream .po, msgstr rewritten; entries whose
    msgstr is empty but whose msgid names the product get the substituted
    English text so the fallback also reads correctly;
  * an English catalog for the source strings in the .pot that name the
    product, so the untranslated UI switches too.

Attribution strings that must keep naming OrcaSlicer are excluded.
The .mo writer is self-contained so the build does not need gettext.
"""

import argparse
import re
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

input.recap: I've sized the job and haven't changed anything yet. The fork's own text is in English only: about 380 new strings in the native windows and about 600 in the web pages, which have no translation support at all. Three decisions need your answer before I start.

content.text:
I haven't changed anything yet. Translating the fork into the same 23 languages as upstream (English plus 22 translations) is a large job, and three decisions are yours before I start.

**What's there today.** If someone sets the app to German, upstream's own windows show German. The fork's windows mostly stay English:

- **Native windows** (the menus, the left pane, the Check print dialog, the printer window, and so on): 33 files already mark their text for translation, about 490 distinct strings. About 110 of those happen to match upstream text and already translate. The other 380 never do, because none of these files are listed in `localization/i18n/list.txt`, so their text is never collected. Some text the native code sends to the pages isn't marked at all; I haven't counted that yet.
- **The web pages** (AI chat, Home, Preferences, setup cards, sign-in): about 600 strings written straight into the code in English, with no translation support of any kind.

That comes to about 1,000 to 1,300 strings, each needing 22 translations.

**What I propose (not agreed yet):**

- **Native windows.** Mark the remaining text and keep the fork's translations in its own catalog files. The build already runs a script, `Brand/brand_catalogs.py`, that builds the translation files the app loads. It would merge the fork's catalogs in too. Upstream's translation files stay untouched, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release brings no translation conflicts.
- **Web pages.** Add Lingui, an established React translation library that pulls text out of the page code into the same `.po` file format. The app tells each page its language when the page opens.
- **AI-facing text stays English.** That covers prompts, skills and tool descriptions; the existing `wording.test.ts` guard already covers that text. The AI keeps replying in whatever language the person writes in.
- **Doing the translation.** One subagent per language, following the repo's translation rules: every entry gets a `# AI Translated` comment, entries I'm unsure of get `# Needs human review`, and every catalog must pass a `msgfmt` check. Then I'd run the app in German and in Japanese and screenshot the main screens to check the result.

**Decision needed: may the 22 languages ship as machine translations with no native-speaker review?** The project has no translators lined up. Shipping them means people will sometimes see awkward wording until someone reports it. Holding each language until a native speaker checks it could take months. A middle path is to ship a few languages now and the rest later. I'd ship all 22, marked as AI-translated. Is that acceptable?

**Decision needed: should the in-app guide be translated too?** The guide is the pages in `docs/guide/`: 7 pages with screenshots. The app shows it in a window, and the same pages also build the AI's guide skill. Translating it roughly doubles the work. The screenshots would still show English, and every release's guide check would have to cover 23 versions. I'd keep the guide English for now and translate it separately later. Do you agree?

**Decision needed: should this start now, or wait for the uncommitted work in the main checkout?** The main checkout has about 60 changed files from the error-handling work. Marking text touches many of the same files, such as `App.tsx`, `Preferences.tsx`, `SetupCard.tsx` and about 40 native files. If I start now in my own worktree, whoever lands second resolves the conflicts. If I wait, nothing conflicts, but nothing starts until that work is committed. I'd wait for that work to land, and meanwhile build only the plumbing, which touches different files. Should I do that?

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

# JusPrin Agent UI

The local React/TypeScript application that renders the Agent conversation
pane inside `wxWebView`. It talks to OrcaSlicer exclusively through the
versioned `jusprin-agent-bridge` JSON protocol whose shared source of truth is
`resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json`; the native side lives in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`.

The page renders native state and submits typed requests. It never owns an
editable copy of the project or conversation: the native `AgentHost` is
authoritative, and every reload re-runs the handshake and reconstructs the
page from the host's `state` message.

## Building

CMake builds this page whenever an input changes (`npm ci` from the lockfile, then `npm run build`). The output is `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; it is generated, not committed. Node/npm is required unless you configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply that file yourself.

```bash
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web
```

The bundle must stay a single self-contained file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`):
WKWebView does not reliably load `file:` subresources.

To point the running app at a Vite dev server instead of the packaged file (hot
module reload):

```bash
cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm run dev
JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 ./build/arm64/src/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
```

Adjust the binary path for your build tree and platform. The environment
variable is read once at construction; there is no settings UI for it.

## Testing

```bash
npm test        # vitest: protocol, bridge client, reducer, and DOM interaction tests
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
"""

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
JUSPRIN = HERE.parent
ROOT = JUSPRIN.parents[3]
UPSTREAM_I18N = ROOT / "localization" / "i18n"
NATIVE = HERE / "native"
PAGES = HERE / "pages"

# The same keywords upstream's scripts/run_gettext.sh passes.
XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS = [
    "--keyword=L", "--keyword=_L", "--keyword=_u8L",
    "--keyword=L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_u8L_CONTEXT:1,2c",
    "--keyword=_L_PLURAL:1,2",
]
# Test doubles and the page projects are not native interface text.
SKIP_DIRS = {"Testing", "AgentUI", "HomeUI", "WebShared", "node_modules", "Localization"}

DATE = re.compile(r'^"POT-Creation-Date: .*\\n"\n', re.M)


def languages():
    data = json.loads((HERE / "languages.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [l["code"] for l in data["languages"] if l["code"] != data["source"]]


def run(*args, **kw):
    subprocess.run(list(args), check=True, **kw)


def keep_if_only_date_changed(path, before):
    """Leave a file as it was when only its creation date moved."""
    if before is not None and path.exists() and DATE.sub("", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == DATE.sub("", before):
        path.write_text(before, encoding="utf-8")


def native_sources():
    files = []
    for f in sorted(JUSPRIN.rglob("*")):
        if f.suffix in (".cpp", ".hpp") and not SKIP_DIRS.intersection(f.relative_to(JUSPRIN).parts):
            files.append(str(f.relative_to(ROOT)))
    return files


def upstream_header_line(lang, name):
    po = UPSTREAM_I18N / lang / f"OrcaSlicer_{lang}.po"
    m = re.search(rf'^"{name}: (.*)\\n"$', po.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def update_native():
    NATIVE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    pot = NATIVE / "JusPrin.pot"
    before = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if pot.exists() else None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp = Path(tmp)
        listing = tmp / "files.txt"
        listing.write_text("\n".join(native_sources()) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        everything = tmp / "all.pot"
        run("xgettext", *XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS, "--add-comments=TRN", "--from-code=UTF-8", "--no-location",
            "--boost", "--no-wrap", "--package-name=JusPrin", "-f", str(listing), "-o", str(everything), cwd=ROOT)
        # Entries OrcaSlicer's template also has keep upstream's translations.
        shared = tmp / "shared.pot"
        run("msgcomm", "--more-than=1", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(shared), str(everything),
            str(UPSTREAM_I18N / "OrcaSlicer.pot"))
        if shared.exists():
            run("msgcat", "--unique", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(pot), str(everything), str(shared))
        else:
            shutil.copy(everything, pot)
    text = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("charset=CHARSET", "charset=UTF-8")
    pot.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    keep_if_only_date_changed(pot, before)

    for lang in languages():
        po = NATIVE / f"{lang}.po"
        before = po.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if po.exists() else None
        if po.exists():
            run("msgmerge", "--quiet", "-N", "--no-wrap", "--previous", "-U", "--backup=none", str(po), str(pot))
        else:
            header = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            plural = upstream_header_line(lang, "Plural-Forms") or "nplurals=2; plural=(n != 1);"
            header = header.replace('"Language: \\n"', f'"Language: {lang}\\n"')
            header = re.sub(r'"Plural-Forms: .*\\n"', f'"Plural-Forms: {plural}\\\\n"', header)
            header = header.replace("#, fuzzy\nmsgid \"\"", "msgid \"\"", 1)
            po.write_text(header, encoding="utf-8")
        keep_if_only_date_changed(po, before)


def update_pages():
    before = {p: p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in PAGES.glob("*.po")}
    npx = shutil.which("npx") or shutil.which("npx.cmd")
    if npx is None:
        sys.exit("update_catalogs: npx not found; the page catalogs need Node")
    run(npx, "lingui", "extract", "--clean", cwd=JUSPRIN / "AgentUI")
    for path, text in before.items():
        keep_if_only_date_changed(path, text)


def main():
    for tool in ("xgettext", "msgmerge", "msgcat", "msgcomm"):
        if shutil.which(tool) is None:
            sys.exit(f"update_catalogs: {tool} not found; install GNU gettext")
    update_native()
    update_pages()
    print("update_catalogs: native/JusPrin.pot, native/<lang>.po and pages/<lang>.po are up to date")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# JusPrin's translations JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for (`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new entry in every `.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's `AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: ` where the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder. The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like `<0>…` for elements inside a `Trans`, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). ## Marking text Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items, tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly as it was. Leave these in English, unmarked: - **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown. - Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes, test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code. - Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`, `report_error`): they are read by developers. - Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names. ### In the pages ```tsx import { t, plural } from '@lingui/core/macro'; import { Trans } from '@lingui/react/macro';

Takes effect when {app} restarts. Your project is saved first.

const label = plural(count, { one: '# printer', other: '# printers' }); const title = t({ message: 'Back', context: 'navigation' }); // a word with several meanings const hint = t({ message: 'Fit', comment: 'Verb: scale the model to the plate' }); // a note for translators ``` - One message per sentence. Never build a sentence from translated pieces, and never splice a translated word into another sentence: use a placeholder, or a `Trans` with the element inside it. - A count needs `plural` / `Plural`, not "printer(s)". - Put only plain variables in placeholders (`{name}`, not `{a.b.c}`): the translator sees the variable's name. Pull an expression into a well-named local first. - The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no provider (see `i18n.tsx`). - Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps working. ### In the native code - `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for JSON sent to a page. - Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs before the language is loaded. Mark such a table with `L("…")` and call `_L`/`_u8L` on the entry where it is shown. - Use `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)` rather than concatenation, and `_L_PLURAL` for counts; `// TRN` above a string tells the translator what it means. - Every file that marks text is extracted: `update_catalogs.py` reads every `.cpp` and `.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` except `Testing/`. Do not add JusPrin files to `localization/i18n/list.txt`.

input.content:
# Translating JusPrin's own interface text into one language

JusPrin is a 3D-printing slicer, a fork of OrcaSlicer, with an AI chat built in. Its own text has two catalogs per language, and you translate both for your language:

- `N` = `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/<code>.po`: the native windows (menus, the left pane, dialogs, Home's native parts). gettext format; placeholders are `%1%`, `%2%` (boost format, may be reordered), `%s`, `%d`, `%g` (printf, order must stay), and `\n`.
- `P` = `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/<code>.po`: the AI chat page, Preferences, the printer form, Home. Lingui gettext format whose msgid is an ICU message: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags `<0>…</0>` and `<1/>` around inner elements, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` (also `=1 {…}` exact matches, and `#` for the number).

Shell working directories reset between commands: use absolute paths. Other translators edit other languages' files at the same time: touch ONLY your two files. Do not commit, do not run `update_catalogs.py` or `lingui extract`, do not change any msgid, msgctxt, comment line starting `#.` or `#:`, or the order of entries. Work directly, do not delegate, never stop to wait, and finish before you end your turn.

## Before you start

1. Read `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/README.md` and the "Localization & translations" section of `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/AGENTS.md` (editing rules), and `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/translation-rules.md`.
2. Terminology: fetch upstream's glossary for your language, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/main/developer_reference/glossary/<code>.tsv` (curl is fine), and use upstream's own catalog `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/localization/i18n/<code>/OrcaSlicer_<code>.po` as the reference for how the app already says recurring words (filament, plate, slice, preset, nozzle, print settings, printer, project, G-code, support, Preferences, Cancel/OK, Undo…). JusPrin's text must read as part of the same app. Grep it for a term before choosing a word.

## How to translate

- Translate every entry in both files: every `msgstr ""` gets the translation. For a native plural entry (`msgid_plural`), fill `msgstr[0]` … `msgstr[n-1]` with the number of forms the file's `Plural-Forms` header says, each genuinely inflected for its quantity.
- Translate the meaning. Read the `#.` comments (translator notes and the placeholder names Lingui prints, such as `placeholder {0}: appearance.restartFor`) and the `#:` source path to know where the text appears. A short label is a button, menu item or heading: use the imperative or noun form your language uses for UI controls, consistent with upstream's catalog.
- Keep exactly: every placeholder and tag (`%1%`, `%s`, `{0}`, `{name}`, `<0>`, `</0>`, `<1/>`), every `\n` (count and position), leading and trailing spaces, and the ICU structure. Translate the words inside each plural branch. This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. **Primary request and intent**
   - **First request:** the user asked how many languages and regions upstream OrcaSlicer supports. Answer: 23 interface languages (English plus 22 translations). Only zh_CN, zh_TW and pt_BR are regional. Romanian is listed in code but has no catalog.
   - **Main request:** "Localize the fork to the same languages". That covers JusPrin's own native text and the AI and Home web pages, in all 23 languages.
   - **User decisions:**
     - Ship all 22 as machine translations marked `# AI Translated`, with no native-speaker review: **yes**.
     - Keep the in-app guide (`docs/guide`) English: **ok**.
     - "do you work in a worktree off of the jusprin-dev branch". Start now, in a worktree from `jusprin-dev`; don't touch the main checkout, which holds about 60 uncommitted error-handling files from other work.

2. **Key technical concepts**
   - **Catalogs.** JusPrin keeps its own catalogs apart from upstream's, so upstream merges never conflict in them:
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/<lang>.po` and `native/JusPrin.pot`: gettext, boost `%1%` placeholders.
     - `Localization/pages/<lang>.po`: Lingui ICU messages, one catalog for both pages, including en.po.
   - **Native merge.** `brand_catalogs.py --fork-po-dir` merges the native catalogs into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<appkey>.mo`, with no product-name substitution (`product=None`).
   - **Lingui 5.9.5,** pinned exact. Lingui 6 needs Vite 6.3+; the pages use Vite 5.
     - Macros: `t` and `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans` and `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro`.
     - `runtimeConfigModule` maps `Trans` and `useLingui` to `@jusprin/i18n`, a Vite alias for `AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`. They use `TransNoContext` with the global i18n, so no `I18nProvider` is needed.
     - The language is activated on import of `i18n.tsx`, from `?lang=`. Each page's `main.tsx` imports it first.
   - **Language passing.** The app passes `?lang=<current_language_code>` (for example de_DE) through `with_page_language()`. `pageLanguage()` maps it to a catalog: exact match, then the base language, then zh with Traditional detection, then English. The BCP 47 tag goes into `document.documentElement.lang`.
   - **GUI-free files.** Files that the tests compile without wx use `Support/Translate.hpp`: mark with `L()`, translate with `translated()`. The translator is installed by a static initializer in `AgentWebView.cpp`.
   - **Extraction.** `update_catalogs.py` runs xgettext with upstream's keywords over the JusPrin C++ (skipping Testing/, AgentUI/, HomeUI/, WebShared/, node_modules/, Localization/). It then drops msgids shared with `OrcaSlicer.pot` (`msgcomm --more-than=1`, then `msgcat --unique`), msgmerges each language, and runs `npx lingui extract --clean` in AgentUI. It keeps a file as it was when only `POT-Creation-Date` changed.
   - **Model-facing text stays English** (prompts, skills, tool results); `wording.test.ts` guards it.
   - **ICU apostrophe trap.** A plain `'` next to `{`, `}` or `#` starts quoting in ICU, so page translations use the typographic ’.
   - **xgettext and TRN notes.** xgettext attaches a TRN comment to the first keyword after it. Each note must sit directly above its own string.

3. **Files and code sections** (worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork`)

   **New files**
   - **`Localization/languages.json`:** `{source:"en", languages:[{code,tag}...]}`, 23 entries; for example pt_BR → pt-BR, zh_CN → zh-CN.
   - **`Localization/README.md`:** the marking and translation rules: what to mark, what stays English, the page and native patterns.
   - **`Localization/update_catalogs.py`:** the extraction above. For a new language it builds a header-only file with upstream's `Plural-Forms`, then `msgmerge -U`, so the number of plural forms is right.
   - **`AgentUI/lingui.config.ts` and `HomeUI/lingui.config.ts` (identical):**
     - catalogs path `<rootDir>/../Localization/pages/{locale}`
     - include `../AgentUI/src` and `../HomeUI/src`
     - exclude tests, `visual/`, `*.visual-cases.*`, `test/`
     - `formatter({ lineNumbers: false })`
     - `runtimeConfigModule: { Trans: ['@jusprin/i18n','Trans'], useLingui: ['@jusprin/i18n','useLingui'] }`
   - **`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`:**
     - `import.meta.glob('../../Localization/pages/*.po', {eager:true})`
     - `pageLanguage(requested)` and `activateLanguage(requested)`, which calls `i18n.load`, `i18n.activate(code, [tag])` and sets the document language
     - `dateLocale(english)`: returns `english` in English, otherwise the document language
     - activates on import from `location.search`
     - `export function Trans(props: TransProps) { return <TransNoContext {...props} lingui={{ i18n }} />; }`
     - `useLingui() { return { i18n, _: i18n._.bind(i18n) }; }`
   - **`AgentUI/src/po.d.ts`:** module declaration for `*.po`.

   - **TRN notes moved** onto the right lines in `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`, `AgentHost.cpp`, `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` (with a new `saved_as` local) and `StatusRow.cpp`.

   - **Lingui needing a provider:** tests render components without `I18nProvider`, and `Trans` throws without one. Fixed with a custom `Trans` and `useLingui` through `runtimeConfigModule`.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

# Any further arguments are folders of another page whose source this page
# imports, so a change there rebuilds this bundle too.
function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    foreach(_imported ${ARGN})
        file(GLOB_RECURSE _imported_src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${_imported}/*)
        list(APPEND _src ${_imported_src})
    endforeach()
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
                ${project_dir}/lingui.config.ts
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

`osascript -e 'tell application "<scratch>/App.app" to open POSIX file "<file>"'` — addresses the copy by its bundle path, so it reaches that instance and not another session's `io.jusprin.JusPrin`. It prints "missing value" and works. `open -g -a <path> <file>` was unreliable (lsappinfo held stale dead entries for the same path); if you use it, add `--args --datadir <scratch>` so a fresh launch can't touch the real data folder.

Do NOT Finder-open a `.3mf` this way: with `single_instance` off, `MacOpenFiles` calls `start_new_slicer`, a second instance on the default (real) data dir.

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what was loaded and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin, each with bedMm, its bed's width, depth and printable height; selectedPrinterBedMm is the selected printer's. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain each dialog's title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. When an object does not fit the selected printer, name a set-up printer it fits, from fitsSetupPrinters.

Write about 80 words, with at most two bullets, about what matters for this file now. The person sees the setup card above your message, with the presets, the plate and the estimates, and the activity line under your turn, with the checks you made: leave those to them rather than restating them.
- Lead with what decides whether or how it can print: a load that failed, an object that does not fit, a printer to choose, settings or G-code that need review. Say it once, with only the numbers that matter.
- Say what you take the object to be, and how it should be printed, only when that changes the advice, and then briefly, as a guess. Leave other advice (material, strength, orientation) until the main decision is made.
- Do not explain routine loading: how the file was opened, whether its settings were applied, or which notices appeared, unless it changes the next step. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.
- When nothing needs attention, say so in a sentence.
- End with exactly one question, about the next step: the message's only question, not a menu of alternatives. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved.

| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |

| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |

content.text:
JusPrin's own text now ships in all 22 languages that upstream OrcaSlicer translates into. That covers the native windows and menus, Home, and the AI chat, Preferences and printer pages. The real app switches with the language setting. Everything is on branch `claude/localize-fork` in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork`, ten commits on top of `jusprin-dev`. `jusprin-dev` hasn't moved since I branched, so it can fast-forward.

**What changed**
- Every language has all 513 native entries and all 898 page entries. They are machine translations, each marked `# AI Translated`, as you agreed. Terms follow upstream's catalog and glossary for each language.
- The translators flagged 427 entries `# Needs human review`. Most are sentences where a name or date the app fills in decides the grammar, the date order, or English that could mean two things.
- The two page files each grow by about 1.4 MB, because every language's catalog is bundled in. They load from disk.

**Three bugs, found and fixed**
- **New chats titled in English:** a new chat showed "New chat" in English in a German or Japanese app, because the app sent its stored English title. A chat nobody has named now goes to the page untitled, and the page shows its own translated title.
- **Squeezed text on the setup card:** in Japanese, "未スライス" broke one character per line and its link ran off the card. German was squeezed onto three lines. The link now moves to the next line when both don't fit. English looks as before.
- **Home build failure:** the Home page could fail to build when the AI page's packages were being reinstalled at the same moment, which a clean checkout also hits. Home now reads its Lingui packages from its own install.

**Tested**
- C++ suites: agent 577, jusprin 240, brand 53 and workspace 51 tests pass, and the shell harness reports 0 failures.
- Page tests: AgentUI 826 and HomeUI 162 pass.
- Catalog checks: all 45 pass, and all 22 native catalogs pass `msgfmt`.
- Live: you declined screen access to the app, so I ran the built app with its pages served locally, plus a script that reported what each page drew. In German and Japanese the app passed the language to the pages, and dates read "12. Nov." and "11月12日". The screenshots I sent are made from those reports.
- Not checked live: the native menus and dialogs. They are checked only through the merged catalog files, which contain the translations.

**Still open**
- "Model" and "Search models" are one string used for both AI models and printer models. Several languages need different words for the two, so the source needs a context added and those two strings retranslated.
- The composer's placeholder is cut off in German ("…oder wü"). The stylesheet keeps it to one line on purpose.
- "Untitled" is still chosen by comparing translated text. That code predates this branch.

**Decision needed**

The printer chat's opening line and the filament chat's greeting are still English in every language. The AI reads both lines as part of its own history, and the app picks the answer choices out of them by looking for the English word "Choices:". You decide what a German user sees there.
- **Option one:** leave them English. That costs nothing, but they're the only English text in those chats.
- **Option two:** show a translated line while the AI still gets the English one, the way I already handle chat notes. That's a small change in two places, plus 22 translations of two lines.

I recommend the second. Should I do it?
Are you done or you're not done? You asked me for decisions, but you also asked me if we should land this on jusprin-dev

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. **Primary request and intent**
   - **First request:** how many languages upstream OrcaSlicer supports. Answer given: 23.
   - **Main request:** "Localize the fork to the same languages". That covers JusPrin's own native text and the AI and Home web pages, in all 22 non-English upstream languages.
   - **User decisions:**
     - Machine translations marked `# AI Translated`, with no native-speaker review: "yes".
     - The guide (`docs/guide`) stays English: "ok".
     - Work in a worktree off jusprin-dev, and don't touch the main checkout's uncommitted work.
   - **Screen access:** the user denied computer-use access to the app (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`). Do not ask again; verify without screen control.

2. **Key technical concepts**
   - **Catalogs.** JusPrin keeps its own catalogs:
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/<lang>.po` and `JusPrin.pot`: gettext, boost `%1%` placeholders.
     - `Localization/pages/<lang>.po`: Lingui 5.9.5 ICU messages.
   - **Merge.** `Brand/brand_catalogs.py --fork-po-dir` merges the native catalogs into `resources/i18n/<lang>/JusPrin2.mo`.
   - **Language passing.** The pages get `?lang=<code>` through `with_page_language()` (`Support/PageLanguage.cpp`), used by `HomeWebView.cpp` and `AgentWebView.cpp`. Dev URLs are `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` and `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL`.
   - **Updating.** `update_catalogs.py` re-extracts. The catalog test `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` checks every language (45 tests).
   - **Bundle size.** Each page bundles all 23 catalogs eagerly, adding about 1.4 MB: the AI page went from 4.3 to 5.7 MB, Home from 1.5 to 2.9 MB.
   - **Live checks without screen control:**
     - Instrumented copies of the built pages are served by `scratchpad/live/receiver.py` on port 8765. An injected script POSTs the page's href, lang, innerText and outerHTML at 5 s and 15 s.
     - The snapshots are stripped of scripts and screenshotted with the Playwright MCP.
     - Playwright saves into `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout), so files must be moved out immediately.

3. **Files and code sections**

   **Commits on branch `claude/localize-fork`**
   - Worktree: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork`.
   - The branch is 10 commits ahead of jusprin-dev, and jusprin-dev hasn't moved since: d8b891ba80, e3131c546b, f13181ce54, 257d3088d4, 6aa166fe91, 19cf140840, d60e8957a7, 4caf1d24f3, 93dee23d8e, 707718399b.

   **`HomeUI/tsconfig.json` (commit d60e8957a7).** Added to `paths`:
   ```json
   "@lingui/react/server": ["./node_modules/@lingui/react/dist/server.d.ts"],
   "@lingui/*": ["./node_modules/@lingui/*"]
   ```

   **`Localization/native/*.po`, `pages/*.po` and `JusPrin.pot` (commit 4caf1d24f3).**
   - All 22 languages: 513 native and 898 page entries each.
   - 427 entries in total are flagged `# Needs human review`.

   **`Agent/AgentHost.cpp`, `conversation_list_json` (commit 93dee23d8e):**
   ```cpp
   // A chat nobody has named yet goes untitled: the page names it in the
   // person's language. The document keeps its English default.
   for (const ConversationInfo& info : document.conversations())
       result.push_back(json{{"id", info.id}, {"title", document.needs_conversation_title(info.id) ? "" : info.title},
                             {"createdAt", info.created_at},
                             {"updatedAt", info.updated_at}, {"preview", info.preview}});
   ```

   **`AgentUI/src/components/ChatNavigation.tsx`.** Added:
   ```ts
   // The app sends a chat nobody has named yet untitled.
   export const chatTitle = (chat?: ConversationInfo) => chat?.title || t`New chat`;
   ```

The search turned up a consistent answer: the Messages API requires the first message to come from the user, but official docs also allow a trailing assistant message.

- **Error behavior:** A GitHub issue in the LobeChat project reports the API returning an invalid_request_error when the history begins with an assistant message, with the text "first message must use the 'user' role" (quoted error message). The reporter found the problem only when trimming message history, and the same history worked with OpenAI's API (the issue isn't happening with OpenAI API).
- **Third-party guidance:** Several non-official guides state the same rule. One says the conversation must start with a user turn and that consecutive same-role messages return a 400 error (messages must alternate, the first message must be from the user, and two consecutive same-role messages return a 400). Another notes the API checks alternation with user first (user and assistant roles must alternate, with user first).
- **Official docs:** Anthropic's own pages describe a single user message or multiple alternating user and assistant messages (you can specify a single user-role message, or include multiple user and assistant messages). They also state that a system message cannot be the first entry in messages and that top-level system is used instead (system messages can't open the array; use the top-level system field).
- **Prefill exception:** The official prompt-validation guide shows synthetic assistant turns in history, and a trailing assistant message is used to steer output (prefill) (synthetic assistant messages are permitted). One third-party guide says a trailing assistant message is optional and makes Claude continue from that partial text (a partial assistant message at the end lets Claude continue where it left off).

Bottom line: an assistant message as the first entry is rejected, while an assistant message at the end of the array is allowed as a prefill. The first-message rule rests mainly on the error report and third-party docs; the official snippets I found don't state it verbatim, so check the current API reference before relying on it.

Lingui's docs support the core approach: give the same text a `context` prop so that identical strings with different meanings are kept apart.

- **Context changes the ID.** The React patterns guide says Use context to add more contextual information for translators. It also influences the ID generation: the same text elements with different contexts are extracted with different IDs.
- **Macro example.** The docs show Trans context="direction" and Trans context="correctness" both wrapping "right", which compile to separate message IDs.
- **Trans and t.** Per the guide, t is equivalent for Trans, plural is equivalent to Plural. The `t` macro is the one to use for attributes such as `alt`, as in the example when translating element attributes.
- **Identical strings without context.** Strings with no context and the same text share one entry. The guide's "right" example says that if the same text elements meet the following conditions, the text elements are extracted only once and use the same ID. That condition is the absence of a differing context.
- **Known issue.** A GitHub-mirrored report from Lingui 3.13.1 described the context is treated like an ID in the generated en.po file when two `Trans` elements with different contexts had the same text. This is an older version, so check whether it still applies to your version.

I didn't find a specific Lingui v4+ or v5+ page on whether context affects catalog ordering or a `msgctxt` field, so verify that in the current docs.

content.text:
**On the greetings:** you're right. I asked whether to translate them, you hadn't answered, and then I described them as part of your request. That decision is still yours and still unanswered, and nothing about it has changed. I've corrected the note I saved for myself so it records this properly.

**On "Model": yes, there's a common practice, and the project already uses it.** It's called a message context: a short label in the source that marks which meaning a word has. Translation tools treat the same word with two different labels as two separate entries. So "Model" labelled "AI" and "Model" labelled "printer" each get their own translation, and a German translator can write "KI-Modell" for one and "Druckermodell" for the other.

- **gettext:** this is gettext's msgctxt field. AGENTS.md already tells us to use it through `_L_CONTEXT` for ambiguous native strings.
- **The AI and Home pages:** Lingui, the translation library those pages use, does the same with a `context` prop. Lingui's guide shows "right" in the direction sense and "right" in the correctness sense extracted as two separate messages ([Lingui React patterns](https://lingui.js.org/tutorials/react-patterns)).
- **Already in use:** the pages' catalog has one such entry, labelled "navigation".

The other usual fix is to make the English itself say which one: "AI model" and "Printer model", with no label needed. It's simpler for translators, but it changes the English on screen. Where the English should stay "Model", the context is the standard answer.

**Where it applies:**
- "Model" is used in Preferences, where it means the AI model, and in the printer picker, where it means the printer model. "Search models" also appears in both senses, in the AI model picker and the printer picker.
- The fix would give each place its own context, then translate the two new entries in all 22 languages.
- I earlier said "Plate" had the same problem. I haven't checked that, so it's unconfirmed.

}
# AI sense, where the plain entry had the printer word.
ai_fix = {'zh_CN':{'Search models':'搜索模型'},'zh_TW':{'Search models':'搜尋模型'}}
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.po')):
    lang=f[:-3]
    if lang=='en': continue
    s=open(f,encoding='utf-8').read()
    blocks=s.split('\n\n')
    done=set()
    for i,b in enumerate(blocks):
        lines=b.split('\n')
        mid=next((l for l in lines if l.startswith('msgid ')),None)
        if mid not in ('msgid "Model"','msgid "Search models"'): continue
        key=mid[7:-1]
        ctx='msgctxt "printer"' in lines
        # The shared-entry review notes are answered by the context.
        lines=[l for l in lines if not (l.startswith('# Needs human review') and ('printer' in l.lower() or 'PrinterPicker' in l))]
        if ctx:
            value=printer[lang][0 if key=='Model' else 1]
            lines=[l if not l.startswith('msgstr ') else f'msgstr "{value}"' for l in lines]
            if '# AI Translated' not in lines: lines.insert(0,'# AI Translated')
            done.add(key+'[printer]')
        else:
            if key in ai_fix.get(lang,{}):
                lines=[l if not l.startswith('msgstr ') else f'msgstr "{ai_fix[lang][key]}"' for l in lines]
            if '# AI Translated' not in lines: lines.insert(0,'# AI Translated')
            done.add(key)
        blocks[i]='\n'.join(lines)
    assert done=={'Model','Model[printer]','Search models','Search models[printer]'},(lang,done)
    open(f,'w',encoding='utf-8').write('\n\n'.join(blocks))
print('ok')
EOF

content.text:
"Model" now has two translations, one for printer models and one for AI models. This is in all 22 languages, committed as 15a967b994 on `claude/localize-fork`.

**What changed:**
- In the add-printer picker, "Model" and "Search models" now carry the context "printer", so they're separate entries from the AI ones. The AI model picker and Preferences keep the plain entries. That sense has more uses, and most languages had already translated it that way, so those translations stay valid.
- The new printer entries use the word each language already uses in "Choose a model". That's 型号 in Chinese (Simplified), 型號 in Chinese (Traditional), รุ่น in Thai and kiểu máy in Vietnamese. Most European languages, plus Japanese and Korean, use the same word for both senses.
- Chinese had both senses wrong before this. It showed the AI word 模型 in the printer picker, and the printer word 型号 in the AI picker's search box. Both now show the right word.
- I removed the Vietnamese and Thai review notes that asked for this context.

**Tested:**
- A new page test switches the page to Chinese (Simplified) and checks that each sense gets its own word. It failed against the old catalog and passes against the new one.
- The AI page's 827 tests pass, including the check that every page entry in every language is translated. Home's 162 tests pass, and both type checks are clean.
- I haven't checked it in the running app.

**Not done:**
- I haven't checked "Plate".
- The greetings are still waiting on your answer.
- The server isn't localized.

name: reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
description: "A failing test with a fake backend is not a reproduction; run the pre-fix code against the real thing before fixing, and say what was and was not seen"

A failing Catch2 test with a fake backend proves the code does what the brief says, not that the bug is real. Before fixing, run the code from before the fix against the real thing, with what the app actually knows printed beside what it says.

**Why:** on 2026-11-01 Kenneth asked whether I had reproduced three printer chat bugs, and I had only fakes for them: "I don't want you to fix the bugs that are in imagination only". The real run then showed one was only partly real as briefed: the "No printer in LAN mode" sentence was true of a printer in cloud mode.

**How to apply:** do it before writing the fix. To do it afterwards, swap production files with `git show <base>:<file>`, keep a temporary harness script, rebuild, and restore from `git show HEAD:<file>`. In zsh, loop over an array: a plain string variable does not split. Run harnesses with cwd in the scratchpad: the Bambu plug-in writes `log_iotc.txt` into the cwd. See [[printer-network-check-harness]].

name: rebuild-wire-request-from-saved-chat
description: "The app saves no sent requests; a chat's request can be rebuilt from current-state.json and the running build's source, minus reasoning items. Includes the 2026-10-30 Orca replay results."
metadata:

  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2f942139-3d5a-4531-83e7-266db91eaa7c
  modified: 2026-10-30T23:57:20.902Z
---

Since 2026-10-30 (commit "Stop naming Orca to the model...") the app keeps each request sent in `<data dir>/jusprin/request-log/*.json`, newest 200, pictures replaced by their size, no headers, no responses or reasoning (Kenneth said no reasoning). Read that first; the steps below are only for chats from before it.

The app did not save what it sent to the model. To replay an older turn, rebuild it:

- Running build: first line of `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/log/debug_*.log.0` names the commit. Read `ProviderAgent.cpp`, `ResponsesCodec.cpp` and `AgentHost.cpp` at that commit, since the wire shape changed in b08a307459 (append-only record).
- Chat: `jusprin/projects/<id>/current-state.json`, `state.conversations[n]` (messages, `chatModel`, `plan`) and `state.toolActivities` (arguments and results, joined by `correlationId` to the message that made the call).
- Workspace block: `resumeCheckpoint.summary` holds it, including `sliceWarnings`; it is saved at the end of the turn, so check it matches the turn replayed.
- Left out of the wire: note messages, and the workspace block of earlier user messages. A note-started turn sends a user message holding only the workspace block.
- A fired skill goes only on its own request (`newest_once`), never on later requests of that turn. print-issues fires by itself on the first request after a slice with new warnings, not only on a chip press.
- Cannot be recovered: reasoning items from the turn's earlier responses, and a skill's picture.

2026-10-30 replay of the "Orca did flag" reply (chat c-2 of p-695f6cbd7c153ebf, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash): gpt-5.4-mini named OrcaSlicer in 1 of 3 replies; claude-opus-5-5 did not in its 1 reply, and 2 of 3 runs called view_render instead of replying. DeepSeek itself has not been replayed. The script was in that session's scratchpad.

Fixed the same day by `with_product_name` in `OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp`, which says JusPrin (the word the person sees in the tooltip); guarded in `test_setting_display.cpp`.
